about.heading: About me
about.p1: I am in my second year of the BI Analyst programme at Nackademin. I model data in a warehouse, pull it from databases, APIs and files, and build interactive reports in Power BI — see the projects below.
about.p2: Before the programme I worked in healthcare, including as a nurse. That gave me a feel for how an organisation runs day to day, and which decisions the numbers are actually meant to support.
about.p3: Now I am curious about how a company your size builds its data models behind the scenes.

project.powerbi.title: Interactive sales report in Power BI
project.powerbi.question: How is a retail company selling — which products carry the margin, and which underperform?
project.powerbi.did: Loaded and cleaned data from a practice database, built measures in DAX, and set up tables, KPI tiles, filters and drilldowns. The layout was designed separately in Canva.
project.powerbi.tricky: The drilldowns — and getting every table and card to interact correctly with each other when a filter is applied.
project.powerbi.outcome: A report where you filter by product or period and immediately see what sells and what underperforms. If I built it today I would start with a data warehouse and do the modelling and cleaning there rather than in Power BI.
project.warehouse.title: Data modelling and a data warehouse
project.warehouse.question: How should a data warehouse be modelled when the source data is spread across more tables than the reports need?
project.warehouse.did: Modelled an ERD and a star schema in draw.io, then implemented it in SQL Server Management Studio with stored procedures and scheduled jobs against the source database. Reshaped the data in SQL — dates into weekdays and quarters, for instance — so it could be filtered on.
project.warehouse.tricky: Holding the modelling, the keys and the naming together all the way through to the final load into the fact table, and then extending it to a snowflake schema.
project.warehouse.outcome: A working data warehouse with the schema definition in draw.io as documentation. Next time I will spend more time on the modelling before implementation starts.
project.pandas.title: A data warehouse in Python and Pandas
project.pandas.question: Can a data warehouse be built and populated in code rather than in the database tooling?
project.pandas.did: Read csv files with Pandas in Visual Studio Code, cleaned the data and built the tables in Python.
project.pandas.tricky: Python syntax, and getting Jupyter kernels and Pandas to cooperate inside VS Code.
project.pandas.outcome: A database built and runnable straight from Visual Studio Code — the same modelling work as in SQL, but in code.
